items.title: Eye To Ad Media Opens a Press Release Network That Routes Each Release to the Local Sites It Fits
items.summary: Every release is now republished on a news site and routed by a public filter to the Colorado and Hawaii sites it fits, with a receipt.
items.content_html:
DENVER, Colo., October 9, 2026 — Distribute Press Releases, the press release service operated by Denver-based Eye To Ad Media, now sends every release it publishes through a routing network. Each release is republished on the news site Action Global News with a canonical link back to the original. A filter then reads the release's industry, location and wording and places it on up to three sites where it fits. The network launches with five sites covering Colorado camping, Denver restaurants, Denver things to do, Colorado community news and Hawaii hotels.

The filter's rules are public. A Denver restaurant opening goes to the Denver restaurant site, a camping gear launch goes to the camping site, and a Honolulu hotel announcement goes to the Hawaii site. Local sites only take local releases. Every placement keeps the original's paid or affiliated label, and every release gets a public receipt listing where it went, with a working link for each destination.

Most small companies pay for a press release and never find out where it went. We built this so every release lands somewhere it belongs, and the receipt shows you exactly where. If a release doesn't fit a site, it doesn't go there.

Zach Wennstedt, founder of Eye To Ad Media.

What a release includes

Each release is published at a permanent address with news structured data, a markdown copy, a claims file and narrated audio when available. It appears in RSS, Atom, JSON Feed and Media RSS feeds filtered by industry and region, and in a company newsroom with an embed for the company's own website. New pages are submitted to IndexNow-participating search engines once they are live. The service does not promise placement on outlets it does not control and does not sell followed links. Links in every release are marked sponsored.

A single release is $99 and includes writing and one editorial pass. Monthly, annual and agency plans are listed at distributepressreleases.com/pricing. A free release builder at distributepressreleases.com/tools/release-builder shows where a draft would be routed before it is sent.

About Eye To Ad Media

Eye To Ad Media is a Denver marketing and web development firm founded in 2012. It operates Distribute Press Releases and a portfolio of local information sites, and builds websites, search programs and custom software for small and mid-sized businesses.

items.title: Eye To Ad Media Begins Custom-Coding AI Agents for Small Businesses, Starting With Lead Response
items.summary: Denver-based Eye To Ad Media now custom-codes AI agents for small businesses, starting with lead response, with a person approving every action.
items.content_html:
DENVER, Colo., October 9, 2026 — Eye To Ad Media, the Denver marketing firm founded in 2012, now custom-codes AI agents for small businesses. The first builds cover three jobs: answering new inquiries within minutes, running sales-trained assistants on company websites, and handling research and content workflows. Every build is restricted to information the business has approved, and a person signs off before anything reaches a customer.

Off-the-shelf agents have become cheap or free this year, and the firm says that is the reason for the narrow focus. General-purpose tools work well when a business runs on mainstream software. The time a small company actually loses tends to sit between its own systems: a field-service CRM, a scheduling tool, a phone line and a spreadsheet that do not talk to each other. A custom agent is built to work in those gaps.

The free agents are good at common work on popular platforms. Most of the small businesses we talk to lose their time somewhere else, in the handoff between a form, a phone and a calendar. That handoff is what we build for, and nothing goes out without a person approving it.

Zach Wennstedt, founder of Eye To Ad Media.

How the builds work

Each project starts with one well-defined task rather than a broad automation plan. The agent gets the narrowest permissions that do the job, read access by default, and answers only from the business's own approved material. It hands off to a person when a question falls outside that material. It keeps a log of what it did and when, and it tells customers plainly that they are talking to an automated assistant.

Lead response is the usual starting point. For local service companies, the first business to answer a new inquiry often wins the job. An agent that replies quickly, asks the qualifying questions the owner would ask and offers appointment times can make that happen at night and on weekends.

Availability

Custom agent projects are scoped individually, and cost depends on how many systems an agent touches and how much testing the workflow needs. Details and a working example are at eyetoad.com, or call 1-800-481-8638.

About Eye To Ad Media

Eye To Ad Media is a Denver marketing and web development firm founded in 2012. It builds websites, runs search and AI visibility programs, and develops custom software for small and mid-sized businesses. The company is based at 1001 Bannock St, Denver, and also operates Distribute Press Releases.

items.title: Aging Safely Baths Publishes a Six-Point Fit Check for Families Shopping for a Walk-In Tub
items.summary: Six measurements to take before requesting a walk-in tub quote, from doorway width to water heater capacity, published by the accessible bathing supplier.
items.content_html:
DENVER, Colo., October 9, 2026 — Aging Safely Baths, a walk-in tub and barrier-free shower supplier operating since 2012, has published a six-point fit check for families shopping for a walk-in tub. The check covers the measurements and household details that decide whether a model will work. The company says most quote requests stall because one of them comes up after a model has been chosen.

The fit check is aimed at the adult children and spouses who usually do the research. In the company's experience, they often start from a product photo rather than the bathroom.

People fall in love with a tub online and then find out it won't go through the bathroom door. Ten minutes with a tape measure saves weeks. Measure first, then shop.

Zach Wennstedt, founder of Aging Safely Baths.

The six-point fit check

1. The alcove. Measure the length, width and height of the space the current tub occupies. Many walk-in tubs are sized for a standard alcove, which can let the existing plumbing stay where it is.

2. The path in. Measure every doorway and hallway turn between the front door and the bathroom. The tub has to travel that route in one piece.

3. Door swing. Inward-opening doors suit some layouts and mobility situations, and outward-opening doors suit others. Note which way a door could open without hitting the toilet or vanity.

4. Seat height. Measure the height of a chair the bather gets out of comfortably. Seat height and depth vary between models and decide how easy the tub is to use.

5. Water heater capacity. A walk-in tub holds more water than a standard tub. Note the size and age of the water heater so it can keep up.

6. The floor. A filled tub is heavy. In older homes, or where the bathroom sits over a crawlspace, the floor is worth assessing before installation.

Availability

Aging Safely Baths supplies Bestbath and ANZZI walk-in tubs and the Bestbath line of barrier-free showers. Fit questions and quotes go through agingsafelybaths.com or 1-800-481-8638.

This is general product guidance, not medical advice. Whether a walk-in tub or hydrotherapy features suit a particular person is a question for their clinician or occupational therapist.

About Aging Safely Baths

Aging Safely Baths has supplied and installed walk-in tubs, barrier-free showers and accessible bathing products since 2012. It is an authorized Bestbath dealer and also carries ANZZI walk-in tubs. The company is based in Denver and serves households nationwide.

items.title: Aging Safely Baths Explains Curbed vs. Barrier-Free Showers for Households Replacing a Bathtub
items.summary: When a low curb is enough and when a true zero-threshold shower is worth the floor work, from a Bestbath dealer that has installed both since 2012.
items.content_html:
DENVER, Colo., October 9, 2026 — Aging Safely Baths, an authorized Bestbath dealer that has supplied accessible bathing products since 2012, has published guidance for households replacing a bathtub with a shower. The guidance covers the choice between a low-curb shower and a true barrier-free, zero-threshold shower. It explains what each requires underneath the floor and who each one suits.

Replacing a tub with a shower is one of the most common accessibility projects in the home. The company says the decision is often made on looks, when the deciding factors are how the person bathing gets in and what the floor will allow.

A low curb is fine for someone who walks in steadily. A wheelchair or a rolling shower chair needs no curb at all, and that is a floor question before it is a product question. Find out what your floor will let you do, then pick the shower.

Zach Wennstedt, founder of Aging Safely Baths.

When a low curb works

A curbed shower with a low threshold suits people who walk on their own or with a cane, especially with a grab bar at the entry. It usually installs without structural work. It can often go into the footprint the old tub occupied, which keeps cost and disruption down.

When to go barrier-free

A barrier-free shower suits anyone using a wheelchair, a walker or a rolling shower chair, or anyone whose mobility is expected to change. It removes the step entirely. It also brings the most structural work:

  • The pan has to sit at or below the floor. That is what makes the entry truly level.
  • Wood-framed floors usually need the subfloor modified to recess the pan.
  • Slab-on-grade floors can require cutting the slab.
  • Water containment shifts from the curb to the floor slope and the drain, so the layout matters more.

What to plan at the same time

Whichever shower is chosen, the company advises installing wall blocking for grab bars while the walls are open. It also recommends a fold-down seat or room for a shower chair and controls reachable from a seated position. Those choices cost little during the project and a great deal afterward.

Availability

Aging Safely Baths supplies the Bestbath range, including barrier-free and curbed showers, shower pans, Crestline wall systems, tub-shower combinations and walk-in tubs. Quotes are available at agingsafelybaths.com or 1-800-481-8638.

This is general product and construction guidance, not medical advice or a specification for any particular installation.

About Aging Safely Baths

Aging Safely Baths has supplied and installed walk-in tubs, barrier-free showers and accessible bathing products since 2012. It is an authorized Bestbath dealer and also carries ANZZI walk-in tubs. The company is based in Denver and serves households nationwide.
